variants.angle: Low-friction one-question hook only they can answer, plus the give for a one-word reply
variants.subject: quick question about {company}
variants.body:
{first_name},

One question. When a new customer finds {company} for the first time, what do they type into Google to get there?

You are the only person who actually knows that answer.

I ask because most US service businesses rank for the words they like, not the words buyers use. The gap is where the booked jobs leak out.

If it helps, I will put together a free written visibility teardown for {company}. It shows where you show up on Google today, which buyer searches you are missing, and the three fixes I would make first. No call required to get it.

Reply with one word, Teardown, and I will start it.

{seo_ps}

variants.angle: Escalate value by showing the placement math the teardown reveals
variants.subject: where {company} leaks jobs
variants.body:
{first_name},

Following up with something concrete.

When a buyer searches for your service, Google shows about 10 links above the fold. If {company} is not in the top 3, you get roughly a fifth of the clicks the top spot gets. The other jobs go to whoever ranks above you.

That is not a branding problem. It is a placement problem, and placement is fixable.

The free visibility teardown maps it for you. Your current ranking, the searches with real buyer intent that you are missing, and the first three fixes in order of impact. It is written, yours to keep, and there is no pitch attached.

Reply Teardown and I will build it for {company}.

If you would rather talk it through, a 15 minute call works too. The teardown is the better first step though.

P.S. I will also flag any pages on your site that Google cannot read properly. Those are silent killers.

variants.angle: Handle the we-already-do-SEO objection and re-offer the give
variants.subject: re: who actually shows up for {company}
variants.body:
{first_name},

Quick one.

A lot of owners tell me they already do SEO. Then the teardown shows they rank for their company name and little else. Ranking for your own name is not visibility. The buyer searching your name already knows you.

The money is in the searches from people who do not know {company} yet. Service plus city. Problem plus near me. Those are the buyers with a wallet open.

I will show you exactly which of those you rank for and which you do not, in writing, for free.

Reply Teardown and it is yours.

P.S. If you handle more than one city or service area, tell me which ones and I will break the teardown down by location.

variants.angle: Managed end to end, zero effort, re-offer the give as the easy first step
variants.subject: you do nothing, that is the point
variants.body:
{first_name},

One thing the teardown will not ask of you: work.

I manage online visibility end to end. The writing, the technical fixes, the Google side, all of it. Most owners I talk to are too busy running {company} to babysit an agency, and they should not have to.

But none of that matters until you see the gap. That is what the free written teardown is for. It shows where you stand, what you are missing, and what I would fix first.

Reply Teardown and I will send it over. Want to skip ahead and talk, just say call.

P.S. I will include a one line summary at the top so you can forward it to your team in ten seconds.

variants.angle: Cost of inaction and competitor compounding, give names the competitors
variants.subject: your competitor is holding your seat
variants.body:
{first_name},

Plain math.

Every month {company} sits below the top 3, the searches keep happening and the clicks keep going somewhere. Usually to one or two competitors who figured out placement first. That compounds. The longer they hold the spot, the harder it is to take back.

{seo_rivals}

The teardown names those competitors and shows the exact searches where they are beating you right now. Free, written, no call.

Reply Teardown and I will get started today.

P.S. Tell me one service line you wish brought in more work and I will dig into that one specifically.

variants.angle: Final value push, make replying trivial, give is the whole deal
variants.subject: still happy to build this for {company}
variants.body:
{first_name},

I have offered this a few times now, so let me make it easy.

You reply with one word. I spend the hours building a written visibility teardown for {company}. You get where you rank, what buyers you are missing, and the first three fixes, on paper, for free. You decide what to do with it, including nothing.

That is the whole deal. No call unless you want one.

Reply Teardown and I will start.

P.S. If now is not the moment, tell me a better month and I will check back then instead of filling your inbox.

variants.angle: Breakup that leaves the give on the table with no call attached
variants.subject: closing the file on {company}
variants.body:
{first_name},

I will stop reaching out after this.

The offer does not expire though. If you ever want to see where {company} actually stands on Google, where the booked jobs are leaking, and the three fixes I would make first, the written teardown is still here. No call, no commitment.

One word, Teardown, whenever you are ready. Could be today, could be next year. The door stays open.

Thanks for the time, {first_name}.

P.S. Even if we never work together, fix this one thing: make sure your Google Business Profile lists every service you offer by name. It is free and it moves rankings.
